cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me a minute. You missed the concert, and I need you to understand why that seat mattered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You knew work might run late. I won't apologise for my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No apology for work. Just hear me about the seat: you'd listened to me practise for months.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed me there because I knew what it meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Can you see why I didn't just let someone else take it?

relationship.evidence: B2 protects a legitimate work concern and B4 offers specific understanding.

heightening.evidence: A5 tests whether B understands why another audience member could not serve the same role.

specificity.evidence: A1 that-seat reference is understandable in concert context, but explicit saved-seat wording would remove an avoidable referent gap.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 asks one direct question based on B answer, rather than explaining a general lesson about hurt.
